segments.name: Client Computing and Physical AI Group
segments.note: PC and client chips (renamed from Client Computing Group); down 5% YoY as the PC market softened, even though Intel says demand for its CPUs stayed robust.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; up 78% YoY — Intel's strongest data-center revenue growth in 15 years, according to its CFO.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $411M of sales to OUTSIDE customers only. Foundry's total segment revenue was $6,697M, but $6,286M of that was wafers sold to Intel's own product groups — counting it here would count the same dollars twice.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mobileye (self-driving tech), the Altera stake and smaller businesses. Intel reports this group at $692M; it is shown as $687M here, net of $5M of intersegment eliminations not attributable to Foundry, so the parts sum exactly to Intel's $16,513M total.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new CPUs, AI accelerators and process technology; up from $3,231M a year ago.

opex.name: Marketing, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and back-office costs; down from $1,129M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: Severance and related costs, mostly from the 2025 Restructuring Plan; Intel excludes these from its non-GAAP results.

oneTimers: A $1,005M mark-to-market gain on Escrowed Shares — Intel shares held in escrow for the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act Secure Enclave agreement — sits inside interest and other, net. It is a paper gain, and Intel excludes it from non-GAAP results.
Gains on equity investments, net were $330M, mostly mark-to-market and price adjustments on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales; also excluded from non-GAAP results.
Restructuring and other charges of $54M are a separate operating-expense line this quarter, mostly severance under the 2025 Restructuring Plan.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Sep 26, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

follow100.label: Client Computing and Physical AI Group

verdict: Intel's revenue rose 21% to $16.5B as data-center sales jumped 78%, lifting operating income to $2.5B — though a $1.0B paper gain on U.S. government escrow shares also flattered the $3.5B headline profit.
otherDetail: Other income of $1,460M combines $330M of gains on equity investments with $1,130M of interest and other, net — the latter is a $1,005M mark-to-market gain on the U.S. government Escrowed Shares plus $461M of interest income, less $324M of interest expense and $12M of other net expense (10-Q breakdown).
footerNote: Foundry is shown at its $411M of outside sales only (its $6,697M segment revenue is mostly internal). Net income attributable to Intel: $3,320M, after $200M for non-controlling interests.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, attributable to Intel; vs $0.90 a year ago

kpis.label: Adjusted free cash flow

follow100Note: Intel Foundry is counted at its $411M of outside sales only (see the segment note); rows are rounded to the nearest cent.

takeaways.title: Data centers are carrying Intel
takeaways.text: Data Center and AI revenue hit $7,318M, up 78%, with $3,039M of segment operating income. Client computing fell 5% to $8,097M — the growth engine has clearly shifted to Xeon servers for AI data centers.

takeaways.title: Foundry still loses money — and mostly sells to Intel
takeaways.text: Intel Foundry booked $6,697M of revenue but lost $1,853M. Only $411M came from outside customers (10-Q); the rest is Intel charging itself, which is why $6,291M is eliminated again in consolidation.

takeaways.title: Paper gains flatter the headline — and explain the YoY drop
takeaways.text: A $1,005M escrow-share gain plus $330M of equity-investment gains lifted pre-tax profit, which is why GAAP profit attributable to Intel ($3,320M) tops the non-GAAP figure ($2,756M). Headline profit still fell from $4,063M a year ago, when a $5,546M gain on the Altera sale swamped a much weaker operating result.
